pill.desc: blue, film-coated, oval biconvex tablet with beveled edges

tell: An oral iron chelator whose boxed warning covers renal failure, hepatic failure and gastrointestinal bleeding.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is about 70% for the oral suspension tablet, and a high-fat meal raises exposure by 18%. About 99% is bound to plasma proteins, and glucuronidation is the main metabolic route.
The active moiety is a white to slightly yellow powder, insoluble in water, with a molecular weight of 373.4.
Approved under NDA 206910 in 90, 180 and 360 mg tablets, with sprinkle granules of the same strengths.

Boxed warning for renal failure, hepatic failure and gastrointestinal bleeding. Contraindicated with an estimated GFR below 40 or platelet counts under 50; diarrhea and rash are the most common reactions.
Chronic iron overload from transfusions in patients 2 years and older, and from non-transfusion-dependent thalassemia in patients 10 years and older.
An orally active chelator selective for iron, binding it tridentately in a 2:1 ratio, with very low affinity for zinc and copper.
The generic name begins with D and has eleven letters.
